review: All six upstream inputs read completely; root MIT applies with no additional file notices. Preserve full notices; public vendor inputs unchanged.

Original clock parent retained unchanged for provenance, never staged runnable. Exact readonly-clock-v1 extraction removes calendar Loader and all calendar forwarding, IPC, refresh, persistence and pointer actions before preparation. Original format/ISO-week/time logic, SystemClock and WidgetButton/OpticalGlyph presentation retained.
WidgetButton and OpticalGlyph unchanged. No registration API; tooltip compatibility callbacks are explicitly inert. Parent/button pointer input disabled; no timezone action or shell.run route.

Commons is a reviewed composition of authored compatibility services and explicitly mapped derived types, not the original full-shell service graph. Palette/font watching and the admitted state adapters have their own boundaries; the pinned English catalog remains en-US rather than full locale-service loading.

TrialShell defaults denied; explicit approved grant before its fixed panel URL; sticky revoke on input change. No arbitrary QML/path/catalog/command. The panel uses pinned Quickshell Variants.model so each connected screen gets one non-focusable bar. A visible Wayland trial stays separately approved; production catalog remains empty.

Clock calendar is a separate derivation (clock-calendar-v2 and clock-calendar-host-v2) of the pinned Panel.qml and BarWidget.qml. The sealed ClockLabel stays read-only. The live trial opens the original month grid. Shell IPC, the timezone helper and upstream shell.json writes are not admitted. Plan 114 adds shared transactional calendar/tray preferences to the existing Appearance store; only field patches are written and host bindings remain intact.

Elsewhen is a derived original panel (Jason Fried, MIT) on centerEnd. Cities and preferences persist in shared, backed-up Omabuntu state (plan 111). Weather fetch, GitHub profiles, notifications and system timezone changes are excluded. Offsets use the read-only helper.

Plan 078: all mapped source parents checked against Omarchy v4.5.0 stable Git blobs. Changed parents and new WallClock reviewed; complete MIT notices unchanged. Original source bytes remain unmodified. The shared Style easing curve comes from stable Commons/Style.qml. Updated transforms retain Ubuntu backend and no-Exclusive-focus boundaries. Weather IP discovery continues through wttr.in, not the new upstream geo endpoint.

Plan 114: calendar field patches and tray choices share the Appearance transaction store; pending projections preserve bindings and newer edits. Dock/display requests are queued with failures surfaced, and keyboard panel switching uses fixed output-local groups. Display cursor functions derive from the pinned monitor source with text size excluded. These repairs are source-only, not deployment or native policy acceptance.

Plan 116: restore original Network details/grid/copy targets/phrase transitions and original standalone QR scrim/speed gauge layouts; new parents are unchanged MIT sources at the stable pin. Ubuntu adaptations use OnDemand focus, pinned interface matrix sharing without plaintext password reveal, bounded sequential Cloudflare phases and no ping/loss traffic. Secondary profile controls are collapsed by default. Source-only; no deployment or native acceptance.

Plan 116 English labels: selected Network/grid/phrase/QR/speed keys are from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omacom/omarchy/ac2690cd7be4f47e4a255f5e2e78d904d436b068/default/i18n/en/shell.json (MIT), SHA-256 c34e291f8309073442ed9d2cfa971877b04c1bd4eaea9462f2f3906fce758584. The full catalog is not staged; the fixed en-US adapter and authored profile-extension labels remain explicit deviations.

Native playback streams are tracked before property reads; frozen primitive rows and ID/name/object-serial guards protect actions and drags. Capture/shell/tuning streams, active-player highlighting, profiles, helpers, OSD and master-input mute remain excluded. Source-only: no deployment or native audio acceptance.
